column1: # The Dynamo parity exclusions (E11-T23 step B, DYNAMO-COVERAGE §7).
# The reverse direction of the parity manifest: of every public member of Spark.Geometry, either a
# row of dynamo-parity.tsv names it, or this file says why no row needs to. A member that is neither
# is counted against the residue budget at the foot of this file.
# IT EXCUSES BY RULE AND NEVER MEMBER BY MEMBER. Spark.Geometry declares 894 public members by the
# manifest's own counting rule - methods, properties, enum values and operators, and not constructors
# or property accessors, and 202 of the manifest's rows name one of them, naming 159 distinct members.
# 234 rows name a Spark member in all; the rest point at Spark.Api, Spark.Geometry.Io or
# Spark.Nodes.Core, which THIS direction does not read (E11-T30, E2-T45). Measured 2026-09-13 after
# E2-T46; the 895 and 130 this header carried before that day were stale and disagreed with
# DYNAMO-COVERAGE 7's own figure. A file of hand-written excuses for the hundreds left over would be the drifting artefact
# §7 exists to prevent. Two scopes do the work - a member-name rule that applies on any type, and a
# whole type Dynamo has no counterpart for - and what neither reaches is counted rather than waved
# through. 37 rules today: 5 member names and 32 types.
# A ROW MAY NAME A TYPE RATHER THAN A MEMBER, and a Done row legitimately does when the capability is a
# construction - Dynamo's Surface.ByRevolve is Spark's `new RevolutionSurface(...)`, and a constructor
# is not a member this inventory counts. Such a row claims the type, so the type may not then be
# excused here. Until 2026-09-12 naming a bare type slipped past that rule silently; E2-T42's
# assessment found it, and the check now catches it.
#   MemberName  Name is a member name, or op_* for the operators. Excused wherever it appears.
#   Type        Name is a full type name. Refused if any parity row names one of its members.
#   Budget      Name is "residue"; Reason begins with the count. The check requires an EXACT match,
#               so the number falls as rows are assessed and cannot quietly climb back.

321 members are named by no row and excused by no rule. Most sit on types that DO map to a Dynamo type, so each is either a member some Unassessed row will name once it is assessed or a genuine gap; a few are Spark's own machinery on a type a row names, which cannot be excused because the type is named, and are counted rather than argued away. The check requires an EXACT match, so the number falls as rows are assessed and cannot quietly climb back. THE HISTORY IS KEPT HERE, because a rise and a fall mean different things and neither should have to be guessed at. 278 to 287, 2026-09-12, E2-T44: assessing DYNAMO-COVERAGE 3.5 named 13 Spark members, which took BrepFaceView, BrepLoopView and BrepEdgeView out of the excused types and moved their remaining members here. 287 to 293, same day, E2-T65: BrepAdjacency arrived, 8 of its members named by rows and 6 not. 293 to 283, same day, E2-T42 step A: 11 more members named by Surface's rows - THE FIRST FALL, and the one the number exists to show. 283 to 291, same step: Surface.ByRevolve names the TYPE RevolutionSurface, because the capability is a constructor and constructors are not counted - so the type is claimed by a row, may no longer be excused wholesale, and its other members join the residue. 291 to 285, same day, E2-T42 step B: seven more members named by NurbsSurface's and PolySurface's rows. Unchanged at 285 through E11-T30 on 2026-09-12, which is the evidence that widening the RENAME-CATCHER to Spark.Api and Spark.Nodes.Core left this direction scoped to Spark.Geometry alone; and unchanged again through E2-T43, whose rows named BrepPrimitives.Box and Cylinder - taking that type off the excused list and adding nothing here, because those two are all it declares. 285 to 292, 2026-09-13, E2-T45: assessing DYNAMO-COVERAGE 3.6 both lowered this and raised it, and the rise is the larger half. Mesh's rows named 8 more of its members - Vertices, Normals, Faces, FaceCount, FaceNormal, Triangulated, Welded and TransformedBy - which took 8 off. But the rows also name MeshTopology.EdgeCount, MeshFace's corners and GeometryJson.Serialize, so those three types may no longer be excused wholesale, and their unnamed members came here: MeshTopology 9, MeshFace 5, GeometryJson 1, measured one at a time rather than reasoned about. A SECOND RISE OF THE E2-T42 KIND, and the same lesson - a type a row names is a type whose whole surface the register has to account for. 292 to 319, 2026-09-13, E2-T46: assessing DYNAMO-COVERAGE 3.8 named 3 more Spark.Geometry members - Curve.BoundingBox, PolyCurve.Segments and CoordinateSystem.ToTransform - and took TWO MORE TYPES off the excused list, Transform (28 unnamed members) and Tessellation (2), measured one at a time. THE BIGGEST SINGLE MOVE THIS NUMBER HAS MADE, and it is the true price of a claim rather than drift: 3.8's transformation family is Done BECAUSE Spark puts the whole transformation algebra on one type, so the moment six rows name Transform.Translation and its siblings, all 34 of Transform's members are the register's business. Excusing it wholesale while claiming it was the contradiction the check exists to catch. 319 to 321, 2026-09-13, E2-T70: Brep.TransformedBy and MeshFace.Reversed were added, and this is the FIRST RISE FROM NEW CODE rather than from an assessment - the check caught them on the first build after they were written, which is what it is for. They are counted rather than named, and deliberately: the parity rows for the transformation family name the Transform FACTORY, because 3.8's argument is that Spark has one mechanism where Dynamo repeats a member per type, so the per-type application members - Curve.TransformedBy, Surface.TransformedBy, Arc.TransformedBy and now Brep's - are counted here exactly as they always have been. MeshFace.Reversed is Mesh.TransformedBy's mirror handling and answers no Dynamo member of its own. A rise with no entry here means a member was added to a mapped type with no thought for the register.
